description_intent: A compliance rule that treats an unencrypted, or attestation-unconfirmed, operating system volume as a failing condition: at every check-in, a device must supply health-attestation evidence that its system volume is protected, and any device that cannot produce that evidence is marked non-compliant until it can.
rationale_intent: Disk encryption only reduces risk if it is actually turned on, and encryption state on an endpoint is not something a central service can simply assume - it has to be reported and re-checked. Turning this into a compliance requirement means a device that cannot produce attestation evidence of its encryption state is treated as unverified rather than trusted by default, closing the gap between a control that was configured once on paper and one whose effectiveness is continuously confirmed on every device that connects.
